map.NH₄⁺ pKa=9.25-0.031×(T-25)；非离子氨占比=1/(1+1: NH₄⁺ pKa = 9.25 − 0.031 × (T − 25); un-ionised ammonia fraction = 1 / (1 + 10^(pKa − pH)); the NH₃ safety threshold is 0.02 mg/L and the TAN safety limit is back-calculated; a measured NH₃ ≥0.02 mg/L is judged over the limit. The nitrite safety limit follows a Cl⁻/NO₂⁻-N molar ratio ≥30: NO₂⁻-N ≤ min(0.1, Cl⁻ × 0.0132), retaining the 0.1 mg/L absolute cap.
Water-quality safety thresholds (this page's implementation, formula-based rather than a lookup): NH₄⁺ dissociation pKa = 9.25 − 0.031 × (T − 25); un-ionised ammonia fraction = 1 ÷ (1 + 10^(pKa − pH)); measured NH₃ = TAN × fraction; TAN safety limit = 0.02 ÷ fraction (from the 0.02 mg/L NH₃ threshold); nitrite safety limit = min(0.1, chloride × 0.0132) (estimated at a Cl⁻/NO₂⁻-N molar ratio ≥30, with 0.1 mg/L as the absolute cap). Validation: temperature 0–40 ℃, pH 0–14, and the other three values ≥0; blank or negative values stop the calculation and clear the previous result. Criteria: NH₃ <0.02 safe, ≥0.02 over the limit (≥0.05 severely over); NO₂⁻-N ≤ limit safe, > limit over.

map.水温 26℃、pH 8 时 NH₄⁺ pKa≈9.219，非离子氨占比约 5.7: At a water temperature of 26℃ and pH 8, NH₄⁺ pKa ≈ 9.219 and the un-ionised ammonia fraction is about 5.70%; a measured TAN of 0.8 mg/L gives toxic NH₃ of 0.0456 mg/L (about 228% of the 0.02 mg/L safety limit, judged over the limit); with Cl⁻ 20 mg/L the nitrite safety limit = min(0.1, 20 × 0.0132) = 0.1 mg/L, and a measured NO₂⁻-N of 0.1 mg/L is exactly at the cap (100%, borderline, monitor closely).

map.为什么非离子氨更毒？: Why is un-ionised ammonia more toxic?
map.非离子氨(NH₃)易透过鳃膜进入血液，毒性远高于离子铵(NH₄⁺)；其占比随 p: Un-ionised ammonia (NH₃) readily crosses the gill membrane into the blood and is far more toxic than the ammonium ion (NH₄⁺); its fraction rises markedly with higher pH and temperature.
map.pKa 在这里的作用？: What is the role of pKa here?
map.pKa 决定 NH₄⁺⇌NH₃+H⁺ 平衡；由 pKa 与 pH 可算出非离子氨: pKa determines the NH₄⁺ ⇌ NH₃ + H⁺ equilibrium; from pKa and pH you can compute the share of un-ionised ammonia in total ammonia, which is central to the toxicity assessment.
